announcements.text: Global Go LLC, Birmingham, Alabama, was awarded a $37,850,000 firm-fixed-price contract to repair failed and failing facility components including HAZMAT, lead based paint, and asbestos abatement. Bids were solicited via the internet with seven received. Work will be performed in Fort Benning, Georgia, with an estimated completion date of Dec. 22, 2028. Fiscal 2026 operation and maintenance, Army funds in the amount of $37,850,000 were obligated at the time of the award. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah, Georgia, is the contracting activity (W912HN-26-C-A030).

Griffon Aerospace Inc.,* Madison, Alabama, was awarded a $17,515,469 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for Outlaw communication subcomponents and training. Bids were solicited via the internet with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Feb. 28, 2027. Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal, Alabama, is the contracting activity (W58RGZ-26-F-A016).

American Ordnance LLC, Middletown, Iowa, was awarded a $12,643,367 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for an equitable adjustment for costs sustained during a shutdown. One bid was solicited with one received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of Oct. 30, 2026. Army Contracting Command, Rock Island, Illinois, is the contracting activity (W519TC-26-F-A552).

Allsteel LLC, Muscatine, Iowa, was awarded a $10,445,516 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for administrative office furniture, including panel systems, wood furniture, fixtures and equipment. Bids were solicited via the internet with five received. Work locations and funding will be determined with each order, with an estimated completion date of May 7, 2027. U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Humphreys Engineer Center Support Activity, Fort Belvoir, Virginia, is the contracting activity (W912DY-26-F-A355).

Northrop Grumman Systems Corp., Chandler, Arizona, is being awarded a noncompetitive, cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost reimbursable, and fixed-price-incentive contract. The total value of this contract is $508,490,719.00. Under this follow-on contract, the contractor will provide flight test support for the remaining Intermediate Range Ballistic Missile/Intercontinental Ballistic Missile targets and integrated logistics support for all government furnished equipment in support of Missile Defense System testing. The work will be performed in Chandler, Arizona; Corinne, Utah; and Elkton, Maryland. The performance period is from September 2026 through August 2035. One offer was solicited and one offer was received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test, and evaluation funds in the amount of $8,786,477.00 are being obligated on this award. The Missile Defense Agency, Huntsville, Alabama, is the contracting activity (HQ0855-26-C-E001).

Pentaq Manufacturing Corp.,* Sabana Grande, Puerto Rico, has been awarded a maximum $763,082,470 fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for physical fitness gear. This was a competitive acquisition with six responses received. This is a five-year base contract with one five-year option period. Other contracts are expected to be awarded under this solicitation (SPE1C1-25-R-0130) and awardees will compete for a portion of the maximum dollar value. The ordering period end date is Sept. 3, 2031. Using customers are Army, Navy, Air Force, Marine Corps, Space Force, and Coast Guard. Type of appropriation is fiscal 2026 through 2031 defense working capital funds. The contracting activity is Defense Logistics Agency Troop Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania (SPE1C1-26-D-0079).

Huntington Ingalls Industries Inc., Newport News, Virginia, is awarded a $336,112,000 cost only undefinitized contract action for advance procurement of long lead time materials to support construction of the future USS William J. Clinton (CVN 82). Work will be performed in Newport News, Virginia and is expected to be completed by March 2039. Fiscal 2026 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funding in the amount of $336,112,000 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was not competitively procured in accordance with 10 U.S. Code 3204(a)(1) (only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements). Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-26-C-2182).

The Boeing Co., St. Louis, Missouri, is being awarded $241,340,000 for ceiling-price delivery order (N00383-26-F-YY2B) under previously awarded basic ordering agreement (N00383-22-G-YY01) for the repair of nine various configurations of flight control surfaces utilized on Navy F/A-18 E/F and EA-18G aircraft. The delivery order does not include an option provision. Work will be performed in Jacksonville, Florida (83%); and St. Louis, Missouri (17%). Work is expected to be completed by September 2032. Fiscal 2026 working capital funds (Navy) in the amount of $60,335,000 (25%) will be obligated at the time of award and funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. An additional $181,005,000 remains committed to fund the ceiling-price delivery order that has a maximum total value of $241,340,000. One source was solicited for this sole-source requirement pursuant to the authority set forth in 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a)(1) and one offer was received. Naval Supply Systems Command Weapon Systems Support, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, is the contracting activity.

General Dynamics NASSCO, San Diego, California, was awarded a $149,599,723 Fixed-Price Incentive Fee contract action for maintenance, modernization and repair of USS Pinckney (DDG 91) Fiscal 2026 Depot Modernization Period. The scope of this acquisition includes all labor, supervision, equipment, production, testing, facilities, and quality assurance necessary to prepare for and accomplish the Chief of Naval Operations Availability for critical modernization, maintenance, and repair programs. This contract includes options, which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value of this contract to $149,921,701. Work will be performed in San Diego, California, and is expected to be completed by September 2028. Fiscal 2026 other procurement, (Navy) funds in the amount of $135,821,005 (91%); fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance, (Navy) funds in the amount of $12,873,554 (9%); and fiscal 2026 weapons procurement, (Navy) funds in the amount of $905,164 (<1%), will be obligated at award, of which $12,873,554 will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was not competitively solicited, but in accordance with 10 U.S. Code 3204 (a) (1) Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N0002426C4401).

L3Harris Technologies, Northampton, Massachusetts, is awarded a $139,012,362 cost-plus-fixed-fee, cost-plus-incentive-fee, and firm-fixed-price modification to previously awarded contract (N00024-20-C-6249) for production of new construction and in-service submarine low-profile photonics masts, spares and engineering support. Work will be performed in Northampton, Massachusetts, and is expected to be completed by September 2030. Fiscal 2024 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $42,247,676 (30%); fiscal 2025 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $19,360,698 (14%); fiscal 2025 national sea-based deterrent funds in the amount of $18,876,901 (14%); fiscal 2025 shipbuilding and conversion (Navy) funds in the amount of $20,038,547 (14%); fiscal 2026 other procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $27,864,934 (20%); and fiscal 2026 national sea-based deterrent funds in the amount of $10,623,606 (8%), will be obligated at the time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Northrop Grumman Systems Corp.-Marine Systems, Sunnyvale, California, is awarded a $111,354,038 firm-fixed-price and cost-only, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity contract for the ship service turbine generator maintenance, overhaul, repair, and long-lead time material in support of the in-service Virginia class nuclear-powered attack submarine fleet. This contract includes options which, if exercised, would bring the cumulative value to $253,293,127. Work will be performed in Sunnyvale, California (40%); Norfolk, Virginia (15%); Kittery, Maine (15%); Bremerton, Washington (15%); and Pearl Harbor, Hawaii (15%), and is expected to be completed by August 2031. If all options are exercised, work will continue through August 2034. No funds will be obligated at the time of the award; funds will be obligated on individual orders as they are issued. This contract was procured on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S. Code 3204(a)(1) only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity (N00024-26-D-4314).

Lockheed Martin Space, Titusville, Florida, is being awarded a $90,229,306 cost-plus-fixed-fee modification (P00030) to a previous award and announced contract (N0003024C0100) for TRIDENT II Life Extension 2 SSP Alteration Advanced Design and Development Program efforts. Work will be performed in Kings Bay, Georgia (68%); Cape Canaveral, Florida (25%); Bangor, Washington (5%); Denver, Colorado (1%); and other locations less than 1.0 percent each, totaling 1%. Work is expected to be completed Sept. 30, 2030. Fiscal 2026 weapons procurement (Navy) funds in the amount of $90,229,306 will be obligated on this modification award and no funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract is being awarded to the contractor on a sole source basis under 10 U.S. Code 2304(a)(1) and was previously synopsized on the Systems for Award Management (SAM) website, with one proposal received. Portfolio Acquisition Executive Strategic Systems Programs, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

Jacobs and Architects Hawaii JV, Honolulu, Hawaii, is awarded a $75,000,000 firm-fixed-price, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, architect-engineering contract for architectural design and engineering services at various locations under the cognizance of the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command (NAVFAC) Hawaii. Work will be performed within the NAVFAC Hawaii area of operations and is expected to complete by August 2031. The maximum dollar value for this five-year contract is $75,000,000. Fiscal 2026 operations and maintenance (Navy) funds in the amount of $3,000 will be obligated at time of award for the minimum guarantee, and funds will expire at the end of the current fiscal year. This contract was competitively procured via the SAM.gov website, with four offers received. NAVFAC Hawaii, Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Hawaii, is the contracting activity (N62478-26-D-5041).

Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems, Moorestown, New Jersey, is awarded a $40,100,000 cost-plus-fixed-fee and cost-only modification to previously awarded contract N00024-20-C-5392 for engineering integration, technical support, material, travel, and depot operations in support of the MK 41 Vertical Launching System electronic systems and computer programs. Work will be performed in Moorestown, New Jersey (60%); Ventura, California (16%), San Diego California (10%); Seattle, Washington (4%); Mayport, Florida (4%); Norfolk, Virginia (4%); and Virginia Beach, Virginia (2%), and is expected to be completed by December 2027. Fiscal 2025 defense-wide funds in the amount of $39,763,333 will be obligated at time of award and will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Sea Systems Command, Washington Navy Yard, Washington, D.C., is the contracting activity.

381 Constructors, Omaha, Nebraska, is awarded a $16,765,241 firm-fixed-price modification to a previously awarded contract for Multi-Mission Dry Dock #1 at Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Kittery, Maine. This award brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $1,959,501,523. The contract modification is for schedule changes associated with vessels moving in and out of the dry dock ahead of schedule. Work will be performed in Kittery, Maine, and is expected to complete by May 2029. Fiscal 2024 military construction (Navy) funds in the amount of $16,765,241 will be obligated at time of award, and funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year. Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Atlantic, Officer in Charge of Construction, Portsmouth Naval Shipyard, Kittery, Maine, is the contracting activity (N40085-21-C-0077).

Healtheon Inc., New Orleans, Louisiana (FA9101-26-D-B008); Edgewater Technical Associates, LLC, Los Alamos, New Mexico (FA9101-26-D-B009); exp Federal Inc., Chicago, Illinois (FA9101-26-D-B010); Burns & McDonnell Engineering Co. Inc., Kansas City, Missouri (FA9101-26-D-B011); Amentum Technology Inc., Tullahoma, Tennessee (FA9101-26-D-B012); Shimmick Construction Co. Inc., Irvine, California (FA9101-26-D-B013); Turner Construction Co., Huntsville, Alabama (FA9101-26-D-B014); and Sea Pac Engineering Inc., Los Angeles, California (FA9101-26-D-B015), have been awarded a $900,000,000 ceiling, indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity, firm-fixed-price contract for facilities acquisitions for restoration and modernization III. These contracts provide for mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, data systems, and controls, and design-build projects for military ground testing facilities. Work will be performed at Arnold Air Force Base, Tennessee; Holloman AFB, New Mexico; Kirtland AFB, New Mexico; White Sands Missile Range, New Mexico; Wright-Patterson AFB, Ohio; Mountain View, California; and White Oak, Maryland, and is expected to be completed by Sep. 4, 2034. This contract was a competitive acquisition, and eight offers were received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $8,000 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Test Center, Arnold AFB, Tennessee, is the contracting activity.

The MITRE Corp., Bedford, Massachusetts, has been awarded a ceiling $626,834,540 modification (P00029) to previously awarded (FA8702-25-C-B001) to exercise Option Year 8. The modification brings the total cumulative face value of the contract to $1,314,100,444 from $687,265,904. Work will be performed in Bedford, Massachusetts; McLean, Virginia; and various locations throughout the continental U.S., and outside the continental U.S., and is expected to be completed by Sep. 30, 2027. This contract involves Foreign Military Sales (FMS) to various countries. FMS funds in the amount of $459,140 are being obligated at the time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Hanscom Air Force Base, Massachusetts, is the contracting activity.

General Dynamics Mission Systems, Scottsdale, Arizona, has been awarded a $99,317,356 cost-plus-award-fee task order for the Mobile User Objective System (MUOS) Ground Infrastructure Segment. This contract provides for the design, upgrade, integration, and deployment of required changes to the MUOS Ground Segment for integration of two MUOS service life extension satellites. Work will be performed in Scottsdale, Arizona, and is expected to be completed by Sep. 3, 2028. This contract was a sole source acquisition. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $23,748,369 are being obligated at the time of award. The Space Force Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Satellite Communications and Positioning, Navigation, and Timing, Los Angeles Air Force Base, California, is the contracting activity. (FA8807-26-F-B008).

Lockheed Martin Rotary Mission Systems, Stratford, Connecticut, has been awarded a $20,314,866 modification (P00372) to a previously awarded contract (FA8629-14-C-2403) for HH-60W repairs. The modification will bring the total cumulative face value of the contract to $6,459,873,127 from $6,439,558,261. Work will be performed at Stratford, Connecticut, and is expected to be completed by April 30, 2027. Fiscal 2025 aircraft procurement funds in the amount of $20,314,866 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center, Wright Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, is the contracting activity.

Leidos Inc., Reston, Virginia, has been awarded a $9,951,332 cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for comprehensive research, analysis, and experimentation on space-based and hybrid communication technologies. This contract provides for scientific, engineering, and technical support. Work will be performed in Reston, Virginia, and is expected to be completed by Dec. 4, 2031. This contract was a competitive acquisition, and one offer was received. Fiscal 2026 research, development, test and evaluation funds in the amount of $60,000 are being obligated at time of award. The Air Force Research Laboratory, Space Vehicles Division, Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico, is the contracting activity. (FA9453-26-C-X020).
